<reason>Side A won the sequencing clash: physical-first still requires travel, timing, childcare, health, and confidence to enter, so it counts only students already able to show up. B's prevention-versus-management and destination arguments were strong, but A answered them with a plausible bridge design and showed digital reach can identify who is missing before physical spaces are built. B never solved the case of students who cannot be present at all.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Most decisive was A's Rebuttal 2: digital help works by phone asynchronously without a quiet room, a lounge solves a place barrier by requiring presence elsewhere, and a room can only notice absence after the repeated attendance that anxiety, shifts, and commuting prevent.</best_rebuttal>
